claim: Try it with sample data opens a separate demo that never changes ordinary game data
sandbox: Fresh browser context; seed ordinary storage, select the landing action, change demo settings, reset, and compare both namespaces.

claim: Play the sample course moves focus to the demo course
sandbox: Fresh /demo; select Play the sample course and assert the course heading receives focus.

claim: Everyone gets the same three-hole course for a UTC day
sandbox: Two fresh browser contexts enter through /demo with a fixed clock and compare the real daily seed and rendered board.

claim: A dotted path previews a shot before release
where: game board, How it works, README
sandbox: Fresh /demo; measure the rendered cyan path before a shot and verify that pausing removes it.

claim: Wind, walls, and the moving bumper are visible during play
sandbox: Fresh /demo; count the cream wall pixels, identify the coral bumper, observe its movement during a shot, advance, and assert the wind label.
Fresh /demo; take and reset exactly five misses, then assert advancement, total count, and the next hole's zero count.

claim: The current run persists in local browser storage
sandbox: Fresh /demo; reach hole two, take a shot, reload, and verify the same hole and shot count are restored.

claim: Sound effects work after a gesture and the sound setting persists
sandbox: Fresh /demo with a recorded Web Audio fixture; enable sound, observe a tone, reload, and observe the saved setting and shot tone.

claim: The game has no accounts, ads, analytics, cookies, or game-data requests
sandbox: Fresh /demo; record methods, URLs, and cookies through play and navigation, allowing only same-origin document and static-asset GET requests.

claim: The game supports drag, labelled controls, Arrow-key aim and power, Enter to shoot, R to reset, and Escape to pause
sandbox: Fresh /demo; exercise Escape pause, zero-length and non-zero drags, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight aim, ArrowUp/ArrowDown power, Enter fire, R reset, and labelled controls; assert visible feedback and shot state.

claim: Sinking all three cups wins; missing a hole produces a distinct loss
where: How it works, end screens, README
sandbox: Two fresh /demo contexts run deterministic three-shot win and fifteen-miss scripts to different end screens.

claim: A winning best score persists in local browser storage
sandbox: Fresh /demo; complete the deterministic three-shot win, inspect the saved best, reload, and verify the winning result remains.

claim: Play again starts a fresh run and keeps the saved best score, completed date, and sound setting
sandbox: Fresh /demo; enable sound, complete the deterministic three-shot win, select Play again, and assert a fresh hole-one run while saved progress and sound remain.

claim: A completed course date persists in local browser storage
sandbox: Fresh /demo; complete the deterministic win, assert the sample date is stored, reload, and assert it remains stored.

claim: Clear local score history asks for confirmation and removes only the best score and completed dates
sandbox: Fresh /demo; seed best score, completed dates, sound, and a current run; cancel once, then confirm; assert only best and completed dates are removed.

claim: Completed win and loss screens copy the date, cups, and shot total without course geometry
sandbox: Fresh /demo win and loss contexts with a recorded Clipboard fixture; assert exact copied text for each outcome.

claim: The game uses fixed 60 Hz simulation and targets 60 rendered frames per second on a mid-range phone
sandbox: Fresh /demo at 390x844 under 4x CPU throttling; assert the 60 Hz simulation marker and measure 120 rendered frames at 55-65 fps.

claim: The complete game is free to play without an account or payment step
sandbox: Fresh /demo; assert the playable Shoot action and absence of sign-in and payment controls.

claim: The production build creates static files with route rewrites and security headers
sandbox: Build and serve dist through the Static Web Apps emulator; open /demo, /privacy, /terms, and an unknown route; assert statuses, metadata, CSP, referrer, MIME, focus, and the 404 shell.
